original_question: Which sets of almost-principal minors can simultaneously vanish for a positive definite symmetric 5×5 matrix Σ, where an almost-principal minor [i ⊥⊥ j | K] is the determinant of the submatrix with row indices {i} ∪ K and column indices {j} ∪ K?
target_in_paper: Section 4, Specific Problem (p. 8): Which sets of almost-principal minors can be zero for a positive definite symmetric 5×5-matrix? The surrounding text makes clear that this is the 5-variable Gaussian conditional-independence realization problem, and Lemma 4.1 gives the paper's explicit equivalence between vanishing almost-principal minors and Gaussian conditional independence. ([citeseerx.ist.psu.edu](https://citeseerx.ist.psu.edu/document?doi=38db4554eb60454d45f6cd8b7d75a190bed051f4&repid=rep1&type=pdf&utm_source=openai))
correct_elements: Your draft is already very close to the paper's actual target: it has the right matrix class (positive definite symmetric 5×5), the right objects (almost-principal minors rather than principal minors), and the right basic question (which collections can vanish). It also uses essentially the same notation [i ⊥⊥ j | K] and the same determinant-based definition that appears in Section 4. ([citeseerx.ist.psu.edu](https://citeseerx.ist.psu.edu/document?doi=38db4554eb60454d45f6cd8b7d75a190bed051f4&repid=rep1&type=pdf&utm_source=openai))
missing_details: The paper's wording is about exact realizable zero patterns: one should ask for those sets S of almost-principal minors that occur as the full set of vanishing almost-principal minors of some matrix Σ, not merely as a subset that can vanish together with unspecified additional zeros. ([citeseerx.ist.psu.edu](https://citeseerx.ist.psu.edu/document?doi=38db4554eb60454d45f6cd8b7d75a190bed051f4&repid=rep1&type=pdf&utm_source=openai))

It should be explicit that Σ is a real covariance matrix, i.e. Σ lies in PD5, the cone of real symmetric positive definite 5×5 matrices. The paper introduces PDn as the cone of positive definite symmetric n×n matrices. ([citeseerx.ist.psu.edu](https://citeseerx.ist.psu.edu/document?doi=38db4554eb60454d45f6cd8b7d75a190bed051f4&repid=rep1&type=pdf&utm_source=openai))

The admissible indices should be stated completely: i and j are distinct elements of [5]={1,2,3,4,5}, and K is any subset of [5]\{i,j}. ([citeseerx.ist.psu.edu](https://citeseerx.ist.psu.edu/document?doi=38db4554eb60454d45f6cd8b7d75a190bed051f4&repid=rep1&type=pdf&utm_source=openai))

To make the question fully paper-faithful and stand-alone, it helps to include the paper's explicit probabilistic interpretation: [i ⊥⊥ j | K]=0 if and only if Xi is independent of Xj given XK for a Gaussian random vector with covariance matrix Σ. ([citeseerx.ist.psu.edu](https://citeseerx.ist.psu.edu/document?doi=38db4554eb60454d45f6cd8b7d75a190bed051f4&repid=rep1&type=pdf&utm_source=openai))

The problem is about labeled variables 1,2,3,4,5, not unlabeled isomorphism classes of independence structures. ([citeseerx.ist.psu.edu](https://citeseerx.ist.psu.edu/document?doi=38db4554eb60454d45f6cd8b7d75a190bed051f4&repid=rep1&type=pdf&utm_source=openai))
refined_question: Classify all subsets S of the family of almost-principal minors [i ⊥⊥ j | K], where Σ=(σab) ranges over real symmetric positive definite 5×5 matrices, i and j are distinct elements of [5], K ⊆ [5]\{i,j}, and [i ⊥⊥ j | K] denotes the determinant of the submatrix of Σ with row indices {i}∪K and column indices {j}∪K. Equivalently, determine exactly which zero patterns S occur as S={ [i ⊥⊥ j | K] : [i ⊥⊥ j | K](Σ)=0 } for some Σ ∈ PD5. ([citeseerx.ist.psu.edu](https://citeseerx.ist.psu.edu/document?doi=38db4554eb60454d45f6cd8b7d75a190bed051f4&repid=rep1&type=pdf&utm_source=openai))
equivalent_formulation: Equivalently, which collections of conditional-independence statements Xi ⊥ Xj | XK, with i and j distinct in [5] and K ⊆ [5]\{i,j}, are jointly realizable as the exact conditional-independence structure of a mean-zero Gaussian random vector X on R^5? ([citeseerx.ist.psu.edu](https://citeseerx.ist.psu.edu/document?doi=38db4554eb60454d45f6cd8b7d75a190bed051f4&repid=rep1&type=pdf&utm_source=openai))
justification: This rewrite stays with the paper's actual Section 4 Specific Problem instead of broadening to the neighboring General Problem. It sharpens your phrase simultaneously vanish into the exact realization problem suggested by the paper's phrase which sets ... can be zero, while importing only the nearby context that the paper itself supplies: the definition of almost-principal minors, the ambient cone PDn of real positive definite symmetric matrices, and Lemma 4.1's equivalence with Gaussian conditional independence. The broader program of studying the geometry of Gaussian conditional-independence models is background in the paper, but it should not replace the concrete 5×5 question your draft is targeting. ([citeseerx.ist.psu.edu](https://citeseerx.ist.psu.edu/document?doi=38db4554eb60454d45f6cd8b7d75a190bed051f4&repid=rep1&type=pdf&utm_source=openai))
